component.name: KuickShare
component.summary: Share files, text and links with nearby devices using Quick Share

description.p: KuickShare is a KDE-native Quick Share client for Linux. It lets you send files to and receive files from nearby Android devices and other Quick Share clients.

ul.li: Send files to nearby devices and receive files from them
Tray icon, desktop notifications and job progress in Plasma
Dolphin context menu entry to send files
Transfer history and trusted devices

screenshot.caption: Send files to a nearby device
Pick the device to send to

description.p: KuickShare now follows the KDE Human Interface Guidelines more closely: clearer labels, keyboard and screen reader friendly links, errors that stay until read and a quieter tray icon.

ul.li: Buttons, menus and titles use the KDE capitalization and wording
Error messages stay until closed and can be copied
The tray icon stands out only during a transfer, a request or a temporary visibility
"Keep running in the background" replaces "Show tray icon"
Links and the "Trusted" mark work with the keyboard and screen readers
A failed pairing can be tried again, and unpairing asks first
The AppImage asks about menu entries in a banner instead of a dialog
Quit is in the tray menu and on Ctrl+Q, no longer in the window menu
No system notification for a finished transfer while the window is in front
Refreshed app icons
Updated translations

description.p: Fixes the Dolphin context menu setting when a package does not ship the menu entry.

ul.li: The Dolphin context menu setting and the entry now agree: when the setting is on and the entry is missing, KuickShare writes it in your home folder at start, unless the package already installs one for all users. Before, the switch showed On with no menu entry in packages that leave the file out.

description.p: A clearer system requirements check for Wi-Fi Direct, and releases checked before they are signed.

ul.li: The System requirements dialog lists each component (Bluetooth, NetworkManager, Wi-Fi adapter, dnsmasq, firewall and, in a Flatpak, its permissions) and says right under it what needs attention and what to do.
When neither sending nor receiving can work, the Wi-Fi Direct switch stays off and cannot be turned on, and Check system requirements… says why. A switch that is already on can still be turned off.
The firewall check asks polkit for the permission firewalld actually requires to open the hotspot port.
The Flatpak checks the firewall permission too: it may now ask polkit (system bus name org.freedesktop.PolicyKit1), only to learn without a prompt whether firewalld will accept the port.
In the Flatpak, dnsmasq cannot be seen from the sandbox: it no longer makes receiving Unknown and is checked when the first hotspot starts.
The Flatpak repository of a release is checked on a machine without the signing key, and the signing approval is asked for only once every check is green.

description.p: Safer receiving, a check of what transfers without a shared network need, and a more responsive app while sending.

ul.li: Check system requirements, in the Wi-Fi Direct settings, shows whether sending, receiving and joining a network can work on this computer and what is missing. The diagnostic report it copies contains no network names, addresses or device names. Turning the option on is refused when neither direction can work.

Receiving through the computer's hotspot opens only the transfer port in firewalld. When that is not allowed, the transfer stays on Bluetooth and KuickShare asks before opening the hotspot without a firewall rule, for this session only. Before, every port was opened without asking.

Trusted devices were recognised by name and network address, which another device on the same network can copy. The list is emptied once with this update and a notice says so; trust a device again from its next transfer.

Received files never overwrite an existing file, are written only after you accept, are removed when a transfer is cancelled or fails, and count as received only when complete. An offer with too many files, or larger than the free space, is refused with the reason.
Connections that stall or flood the computer are timed out and limited, so receiving keeps working.
An answer goes to the transfer it was given for: an old notification can no longer accept a newer transfer.
Cancel works while a send is still looking for the device, and the app no longer waits during that search. Quitting restores the previous Wi-Fi connection in time.
Settings, history and pairings are saved safely and are readable only by you; a file that cannot be read is kept aside instead of being overwritten.
Preferences from the tray menu opens the settings when the window is closed, instead of the Send page.

description.p: Join a Wi-Fi network from a phone, temporary visibility, folders, and command-line sending to a named device.

ul.li: Join a Wi-Fi network received from a phone. The password is kept in memory for 10 minutes and never written to disk.
Visible for 10 minutes from the tray menu.
Send folders: they are sent as their files, without their structure. Hidden files and symbolic links are skipped.
kuickshare --device "name" files... sends to one nearby device with that name.
Open each received file from the transfer details, and see the speed and time left of a running transfer.
The history keeps the newest 1000 entries.
Accept and Decline no longer wait while a send chooses its route.
Fixes: received files with the same name no longer overwrite each other; an unreadable identity file keeps the pairings; a failed send is cancelled in the library; discovery resumes after a restart.

description.p: Fixes computers not seeing each other.

ul.li: Since 1.3.2 the computer was no longer announced on the network, so phones and other computers could not see it. It is announced again.

description.p: Search and filters on the Transfers page, and cleaner messages.

ul.li: The Transfers page has a search field (Ctrl+F) that matches the device name, received text and file names, and menus to show only received or sent transfers, and only transfers in progress, completed or not completed. Reset filters brings the whole list back.
The message boxes show their icon centered, and their texts no longer end with a period.
The default device name is read straight from the system hostname and falls back to "Unknown device" when it is empty.
KuickShare no longer uses the AGPL-3.0 licensed sys_metrics library, nor the unmaintained gcc and mach crates.
Translations are updated; the Dutch and Turkish ones have not been reviewed by a native speaker.
